Issued at 203 AM CDT Thu Oct 22 2026

Strong upper level ridging will remain over the central portion
of the U.S. through Friday. This will bring a couple of
unseasonably warm days to western and central ND. Near record
highs are possible today, and especially Friday, before much
cooler air arrives for the weekend and into the first half of
next week. 

Today will be breezy at times and Friday will be breezy to 
windy with south to southeast winds across the forecast area
both days. Forecast highs are in the 70s today and 70s to lower
80s southwest on Friday. If these forecast highs hold, 
Dickinson and Bismarck could both see a record high Friday. 
That's after a possible record warm overnight low temperature 
Friday morning as well. We utilized a blend of NBM and NBM90 
both today and Friday for forecast highs.

Dry conditions are expected today through tonight. Friday may 
bring a passing shower, but most will remain dry. Pops Friday 
are pretty much nil across the area during the day, with a 
little better chance of some wrap around moisture making it into
the northwest Friday night. The threat for thunder looks to be 
lower than it was yesterday. Although it can not be completely 
ruled out, will not carry a mention of thunder in the forecast 
Friday.

The main forecast concerns will be fire weather Friday
afternoon, then wind highlights may be needed Friday night and
Saturday. 

An upper level trough will lift through the Northern Rockies 
Friday and close off over central Saskatchewan by 12Z Saturday
and then track east into Manitoba during the day Saturday. On
Friday, surface cyclogenesis takes place over then northern 
High Plains, with good model agreement in a surface low depicted
along the Montana/North Dakota border by 00 UTC Saturday. A 
south to southeast surface flow over ND during the day, is 
forecast to turn southwest over the Mondak region Friday 
afternoon, ahead of the surface low, advecting much drier air 
into southwest ND. Surface winds are not all that strong but 
there is an 850 mb jet propagating into southwest ND and with 
strong daytime heating, we should see some steep lapse rates 
and a good mixdown potential for a few hours Friday afternoon. 
This scenario has been pretty consistent for the past couple of 
days, but it's a pretty small area of southwest ND that could be
impacted. If the system slows just a bit, the southwest may 
miss out on the good mixdown winds Friday afternoon. The trend 
has been there long enough though, to introduce some near 
critical fire weather conditions friday afternoon. For now, will
keep with near critical "possible". If the trend does hold, a 
small area (mainly portions of Bowman and Slope Counties) could 
see a few hours of critical fire weather conditions. For now 
will go with near critical possible and include the surrounding 
counties as well.

The system moves quickly northeast into southern Canada by
Saturday morning, and continues to intensify during the day as
it lifts into central/northern Manitiba by Saturday evening.
This will bring a strong, but dry cold front through the sate
Friday night. There is a strong fall-rise couplet that lifts
across the forecast area Friday night, along with a period of
strong cold advection at the surface and aloft, and a period of
unidirectional winds through 850 mb and steep lapse rates to 
around 850-800 mb. Bufkit soundings indicate winds around 45-52 
knots at the top of the boundary layer, with a reasonably well 
mixed boundary layer. The question is whether or not these 
strong winds can mix down to the surface. During the peak 
heating of the day, this would be a much easier question. With 
the timing being during the overnight and early morning hours, 
the strong cold advection, gradient winds and isallobaric 
component will need to overcome the tendency for the boundary 
layer to decouple. We've got a while yet to decide on any 
headlines, but would expect a Wind Advisory will be needed for 
portions of the forecast area (west and north central favored) 
Friday night. A High Wind Warning can not be rule out either. 
Another issue will be how long to continue any headlines on 
Saturday. The main push will be Friday night. The southwest 
portion of the state will be the first to see a weakening of 
gradient winds and cold advection. However, with the strong 
surface low spinning over Canada, northern and eastern portions 
of the forecast area could see a bit of a lull in the winds 
Saturday morning, with winds picking up again in the afternoon. 
Certainly something we will need to monitor. For now will 
increase our messaging for winds Friday night into Saturday. We 
also blended in some higher winds Friday night into Saturday 
morning. 

After Saturday, we remain cool into next week. A closed upper
low to our south and another upper low to our west will need to
be monitored. However, at this time the NBM is only depicting
some low pops early to mid workweek as there remains a lot of
